title: Rashtrakuta Dynasty
capsule: The Rashtrakuta dynasty dominated the Deccan plateau and periodically controlled much of the Indian subcontinent from 753 to 982, founded when Dantidurga overthrew the Chalukya ruler of Badami and established a capital eventually fixed at Manyakheta (near modern Gulbarga). An Arab geographer of the 10th century ranked them among the four principal powers of the world; their military reach extended to the Gangetic plain during campaigns against the Gurjara-Pratiharas and Palas, and the empire's cultural apogee under the polymath Amoghavarsha I (r. 814–78) produced early Kannada literature including the Kavirajamarga. The Kailasanatha rock-cut temple at Ellora, commissioned by Krishna I in the 8th century, remains the dynasty's most celebrated monument. The dynasty collapsed after the Malwa king Siyaka Harsha sacked their capital in 972, and Tailapa II of the Western Chalukyas extinguished the last Rashtrakuta ruler around 982.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core Deccan territory is well-documented through copper-plate grants (tamrashasana), inscriptions at Ellora and elsewhere, and corroborating Arab accounts; campaign-era territorial extensions into northern India are transient and the dataset geometry likely represents maximum claimed extent rather than continuous administration.
